title: A World Map & Journeys
strapline: Where in the world? Find it on the map and set off on a journey.
intent: A big world map gives children a first sense that the world is vast, varied and full of places people come from and travel to.
Finding where families come from, where things live and where stories are set builds real knowledge and belonging.
Planning journeys — by plane, boat, train, car — links to transport, distance and sequencing.
Talking about places children have been or have family honours every child's story and heritage.
The map becomes a springboard for small-world travel, storytelling and curiosity about the world.
implementation: Put up a large, simple world map at child height with photos, animals and small figures to place on it.
Wonder together: 'Where does our family come from? Where does the polar bear live? How would we get there?'
Invite children and families to mark places that matter to them — home, family, holidays, heritage.
Plan pretend journeys: 'To get there, would we fly, sail or drive? How long might it take?'
Feed in knowledge lightly — hot and cold places, near and far, land and sea — without overloading.
Follow the play — some children will pore over the map, others will set off on grand small-world journeys.
key_questions: Where in the world does your family come from?
How could we travel all the way there — by plane, boat or train?
Which places are hot, and which are cold and snowy?
Where does this animal live — can you find it on the map?
Is that place near to us, or very far away?

impact.text: Children find and talk about places on the map that matter to them and their families.
Children show respect and curiosity for the many places people come from.
Children plan journeys and talk about transport, distance and near and far.
Children use the map for small-world travel and storytelling.
Children ask real questions about the world and expect real answers.

enhancements: A large floor or wall world map with animals, photos and small figures to place.
A 'where we come from' family display marking children's heritage and travels.
A journeys role-play with a plane, boat and train and tickets to faraway places.
A globe to spin and explore alongside the flat map.
Story books set in different countries linked to places on the map.

playing_exploring: Children explore the map, placing animals and figures and setting off on journeys.
They follow their curiosity about places near and far.
active_learning: Children plan and carry through a pretend journey across the world.
They keep searching the map until they find the place they want.
creating_thinking: Children reason about distance, transport and how to reach a place.
They connect the map to their own family, stories and animals they know.
